Two-term silting and τ \tau -cluster morphism categories
Erlend D. Børve

Abstract
. We generalise τ \tau -cluster morphism categories to the setting of non-positive dg algebras with finite dimensional cohomology in all degrees. The compatibility of silting reduction with support τ \tau -tilting reduction will be an essential ingredient when linking our definition to those of Buan–Marsh and Buan–Hanson.



2020 Mathematics Subject Classification
16G10, 18E10, 18E30

0.
Introduction

In tilting theory, it is valuable to find all tilting modules over a fixed finite dimensional algebra
{\Lambda}
, or better still, all tilting objects in the bounded homotopy category
\Kb(\proj{\Lambda})
, where
\proj{\Lambda}
is the category of finitely generated projective
A
-modules. If all tilting objects in
\Kb(\proj{\Lambda})
could be identified, one could construct all finite dimensional algebras
{\Gamma}
that are derived Morita equivalent to
{\Lambda}

[
Ric89
]
, which is to say that their derived categories are equivalent as triangulated categories. Many invariants of finite dimensional algebras are preserved by derived Morita equivalence, and it might be more efficient to compute these for some
{\Gamma}
rather than for
{\Lambda}
directly.

Finding all tilting objects turns out to be an unrealistic project in general. However, one could instead study the larger class of silting objects, for which there is a mutation process generating new examples in a reliable manner
[
AI12
]
. In addition, one has a reduction procedure for silting objects. Iyama–Yang show that if
P
is a presilting object of
\Kb(\proj{\Lambda})
, then the (pre)silting objects in
\Kb(\proj{\Lambda})
having
P
as a direct summand bijectively correspond to the (pre)silting objects in the Verdier quotient
\Kb(\proj{\Lambda})/\thick(P)

[
IY18
, Theorem 3.7]
.
The class of two-term silting objects closely resembles that of tilting modules. Indeed, a generalisation of the Brenner–Butler Theorem applies
[
BZ16
, Theorem 1.1]

[
BZ24
, Theorem 2.1]
. Also, when performing silting reduction with respect to a two-term presilting object, one can restrict Iyama–Yang’s bijection to a bijection of two-term (pre)silting objects
[
Jas15
, Proposition 4.11]
.

The mutation of two-term silting objects is closely tied to cluster combinatorics. For path algebras of a quiver of simply laced Dynkin type, the two-term silting objects of the bounded homotopy category are in bijection with the cluster-tilting objects in the cluster category
[
AIR14
, Theorem 4.1]
. Moreover, this bijection respects the mutation processes for cluster-tilting objects
[
AIR14
, Corollary 4.8]
. Cluster-tilting objects are in turn in bijection with the clusters of the corresponding cluster algebra
[
BMR+06
, Corollary 4.4]
.

One may also model cluster combinatorics using
\tau
-tilting theory
[
AIR14
]
. Adachi–Iyama–Reiten define support
\tau
-tilting modules and
\tau
-rigid pairs, and show that they correspond bijectively with two-term silting objects and two-term presilting objects, respectively
[
AIR14
, Theorem 3.2]
. The reduction procedure of Iyama–Yang is transferable to
\tau
-tilting theory. Indeed, given any finite dimensional algebra, Jasso provides a suitable bijection between classes of support
\tau
-tilting modules
[
Jas15
, Theorem 3.16]
, and shows that it is compatible with Iyama–Yang’s silting reduction
[
Jas15
, Theorem 4.12(b)]
. Buan–Marsh later extended Jasso’s bijection to
\tau
-rigid pairs
[
BM21
, Theorem 3.6]
.

The bijection of Buan–Marsh was constructed in order to define the
\tau
-cluster morphism category of a
\tau
-tilting finite algebra. This builds on Igusa–Todorov’s cluster morphism category, which is defined for representation finite hereditary algebras
[
IT17
, Section 1]
, as well as a categorification of non-crossing partitions
[
Igu14
]
.
The definition of
\tau
-cluster morphism categories has recently been extended to all finite dimensional algebras
[
BH23
]
. Although Buan–Marsh define the
\tau
-cluster morphism category in terms of
\tau
-tilting theory, they occasionally translate the setting to two-term silting in order to prove necessary results.

\tau
-cluster morphism categories are useful in the study of picture groups and picture spaces, defined by Igusa–Todorov–Weyman
[
ITW16
]
. In the case of representation finite hereditary algebras, we have that the geometric realisation of the
\tau
-cluster morphism category is a
K(\pi,1)
for the corresponding picture group
[
IT17
, Theorem 3.1]
. This result was later extended to include Nakayama algebras
[
HI21
, Theorem 4.16]
.

Outline.

Section

1
sets up the notation and covers the necessary preliminaries. We review how t-exact subcategories (see
Definition

1.5
) of a triangulated category with a bounded t-structure correspond with wide subcategories in the heart (
Theorem

1.10
), the interaction between two-term silting and
\tau
-tilting theory, and
\tau
-tilting reduction. In particular, we recall in
1.18
that a
\tau
-rigid pair
(M,Q)
in
\fgMod({\Lambda})
, where
\Lambda
is a finite dimensional algebra, gives rise to a wide subcategory
J(M,Q)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}M^{\perp}\cap{{}^{\perp}(\tau M)}\cap Q^{\perp}
of
\fgMod({\Lambda})
.

In
Section

2
, we work over a non-positive dg algebra
A
such that
H^{i}A
is finite dimensional for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
. Let
\Der_{\rm fd}(A)
be the subcategory of the derived category
\Der(A)
spanned by complexes of finite dimensional total cohomology. In
Proposition

2.8
(
2
), we show that a two-term presilting object
P\in\per(A)
determines a t-exact subcategory

P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{\rm fd}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}\{X\in\Der_{\rm fd}(A)\,\,|\,\,\Hom_{\Der(A)}(P,\Sigma^{i}X)=0\,\,\forall i\in\mathbb{Z}\}

of
\Der_{\rm fd}(A)
. By
Proposition

2.9
(
1
), the subcategory
P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}{\cap\fgMod H^{0}A\subseteq\fgMod H^{0}A}
is equal to the
J(M,Q)
, where
(M,Q)
is the
\tau
-rigid pair corresponding to
P
(see
Theorem

1.17
).

Section

3
presents a proof that Iyama–Yang’s silting reduction is compatible with Buan–Marsh’s support
\tau
-tilting reduction, generalising Jasso’s compatibility result
[
Jas15
, Theorem 4.12(b)]
.

Theorem
3.5
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a Hom-finite Krull–Schmidt triangulated category and
{S}
be a silting object in
\mathcal{C}
.
Consider a
2_{S}
-term presilting object
P
, let
{\Lambda}=\End_{\mathcal{C}}({S})
, let
T^{+}_{P}
be the Bongartz completion of
P
(defined by the triangle (
1.C
)), let
\mathcal{Z}_{P}={{}^{\perp_{>0}}P}\cap{P^{\perp_{>0}}}
, and let
{\Gamma}
be the
\tau
-tilting reduction of
{\Lambda}
with respect to the
\tau
-rigid pair in
\fgMod({\Lambda})
corresponding to
P
. We have a commutative diagram of bijections
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 2_{S}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}_{{P}}(\mathcal{C})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\staurigidpair_{H_{S}({P})}({\Lambda})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 2_{T^{+}_{P}}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(\mathcal{Z}_{P}/[{P}])}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\staurigidpair({\Gamma})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H_{{S}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{P}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{H_{S}({P})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H_{T^{+}_{P}}}

where
\varphi_{P}
is the Iyama–Yang bijection and
\psi_{H_{S}({P})}
is the Buan–Marsh bijection. The horizontal maps are the bijections between two-term presilting objects and
\tau
-rigid pairs (see
Theorem

1.17
).

Our main result appears in
Section

4
. Given a non-positive dg algebra
A
such that
H^{i}A
is finite dimensional for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
, we construct a category
\tcmc_{A}
, which we call the
\tau
-cluster morphism category
of
A
. Developing the theory purely in terms of two-term silting, as opposed to
\tau
-tilting, has a major advantage; since silting reduction is induced by a functor, it is easier to prove that the composition law in
\tcmc_{A}
is associative, as we do in
Theorem

4.3
.
When we claim that the work of Buan–Marsh and Buan–Hanson has been generalised, it is in the following specific sense.

Theorem
4.4
.

Let
A
be a non-positive dg algebra such that
H^{i}A
is finite dimensional for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
, and let
\tcmc^{\rm BM}_{H^{0}A}
be the
\tau
-cluster morphism category (as defined by Buan–Hanson
[
BH23
]
) of the zeroth cohomology of
A
.
There is an equivalence of categories

.

1.
Notation and preliminaries

Throughout, all subcategories we consider will be full and closed under isomorphism. We fix a field
k
, and declare all triangulated categories and their (not necessarily triangulated) subcategories to be
k
-linear. A
k
-linear category
\mathcal{C}
is
Hom-finite
if the Hom-spaces
\mathcal{C}({X},{X}^{\prime})
(alternatively denoted
\Hom_{\mathcal{C}}({X},{X}^{\prime})
) are finite dimensional for all
X,X^{\prime}\in\mathcal{C}
. It is
Krull–Schmidt
if any object
{X}\in\mathcal{C}
is isomorphic to a finite direct sum
\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}{X}_{i}
, where the endomorphism
k
-algebra of each
{X}_{i}
is a local. An object in a Krull–Schmidt
k
-linear category with a local endomorphism
k
-algebra is called
indecomposable
.

Recall that a triangulated subcategory is
thick
if it is closed under direct summands.
For a triangulated category
\mathcal{T}
, we write
\thick_{\mathcal{T}}(\mathcal{X})
for the smallest thick subcategory containing the subcategory
\mathcal{X}
, or simply
\thick(\mathcal{X})
when there is no risk of confusion.

All modules are right modules, unless otherwise specified. For a
k
-algebra
{\Lambda}
, the category of finitely generated right
{\Lambda}
-modules will be denoted by
\fgMod{\Lambda}
, and the category of finitely generated projective right
R
-modules by
\proj{\Lambda}
. The triangulated category
\Der_{{\rm fd}}(\fgMod{\Lambda})
is the bounded derived category of the former, whereas
\Kb(\proj{\Lambda})
is the bounded homotopy category of the latter. They are both subcategories of the derived category
\Der({\Lambda})
. More generally, if
A
is a differential graded (henceforth
dg
)
k
-algebra
A
, we denote its derived category by
\Der(A)
, define
\per(A)
to be the thick closure of
A
in
\Der(A)
, and
\Der_{\rm fd}{(A)}
to be the (thick) subcategory of
\Der(A)
spanned by complexes with finite dimensional total cohomology. A dg
k
-algebra
A
is said to be
non-positive
if the cohomology
k
-vector spaces
H^{i}A
vanish for all
i>0
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a
k
-linear category and let
\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathcal{C}
be a full subcategory. The
additive closure
of
\mathcal{X}
is the full subcategory of
\mathcal{C}
consisting of all finite direct sums of direct summands of objects in
\mathcal{X}
. We denote this category by
\add(\mathcal{X})
, or by
\add(X)
if
\mathcal{X}
contains only a single object
X
.

Let
\mathcal{P}
be an additive subcategory of
\mathcal{C}
. A morphism

) is
\mathcal{P}
-epic
(resp.
\mathcal{P}
-monic
) if the induced morphism
{\mathcal{C}}(P,\beta)
(resp.
{\mathcal{C}}(\alpha,P)
) is surjective for all objects
P\in\mathcal{P}
. It is a
right
\mathcal{P}
-approximation
of
Y
(resp.
left
\mathcal{P}
-approximation
of
X
) if, in addition, we have that
Q\in\mathcal{P}
. We say that
\mathcal{P}
is a
contravariantly finite subcategory
(resp.
covariantly finite subcategory
) of
\mathcal{C}
if every object in
\mathcal{C}
admits a right (resp. left)
\mathcal{P}
-approximation. A
functorially finite subcategory
of
\mathcal{C}
is one that is both contravariantly and covariantly finite.

The
left
and
right perpendicular subcategories
of
\mathcal{P}
in
\mathcal{C}
are the full subcategories

\displaystyle{{}^{\perp}\mathcal{P}}

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}\{X\in\mathcal{C}\,\,|\,\,{\mathcal{C}}(X,\mathcal{P})=0\},

\displaystyle{\mathcal{P}^{\perp}}

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}\{Y\in\mathcal{C}\,\,|\,\,{\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{P},Y)=0\},

respectively. If
\mathcal{P}=\add(P)
for some object
P\in\mathcal{C}
, we write
{{}^{\perp}P}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}{{}^{\perp}(\add(P))}
and
{P^{\perp}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}(\add(P))^{\perp}
, respectively.

If
\mathcal{T}
is a triangulated category, we denote its suspension functor by
\Sigma
, unless otherwise specified. Let
\mathcal{P}
be an additive subcategory of
\mathcal{T}
. For each subset
I\subseteq\mathbb{Z}
, we define the
left and right perpendicular subcategories

\displaystyle{{}^{\perp_{I}}\mathcal{P}}

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}\{X\in\mathcal{T}\,\,|\,\,{\mathcal{T}}(X,\Sigma^{i}\mathcal{P})=0\quad\forall i\in I\},

(1.A)

\displaystyle{\mathcal{P}^{\perp_{I}}}

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}\{Y\in\mathcal{T}\,\,|\,\,{\mathcal{T}}(\mathcal{P},\Sigma^{i}Y)=0\quad\forall i\in I\},

respectively. If
\mathcal{P}=\add(P)
for some object
P\in\mathcal{C}
, we write
{{}^{\perp_{I}}P}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}{{}^{\perp_{I}}(\add(P))}
and
{P^{\perp_{I}}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}(\add(P))^{\perp_{I}}
, respectively. In the case where
I
is the subset of
\mathbb{Z}
consisting of positive (resp. non-positive, resp. non-zero) integers, we replace the subscript
I
by
>0
(resp.
\leq 0
, resp.
\neq 0
), which for example introduces the notation
\mathcal{P}^{\perp_{>0}}
(resp.
\mathcal{P}^{\perp_{\leq 0}}
, resp.
\mathcal{P}^{\perp_{\neq 0}}
) for the right perpendicular subcategory in question.

Suppose that
\mathcal{T}
is triangulated and let
\mathcal{P}_{1}
and
\mathcal{P}_{2}
be additive subcategories of
\mathcal{T}
. The
category of extensions of
\mathcal{P}_{2}
in
\mathcal{P}_{1}
(also known as the
Verdier product
of
\mathcal{P}_{1}
and
\mathcal{P}_{2}
) is the full subcategory
\mathcal{P}_{1}*\mathcal{P}_{2}
of
\mathcal{T}
consisting of the objects
E
that fit in a triangle
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma X_{1},}

where
X_{1}\in\mathcal{P}_{1}
and
X_{2}\in\mathcal{P}_{2}
. It can be shown using the octahedral axiom that
*
is an associative operation
[
BBD82
, Lemme 1.3.10]
.
A full subcategory
\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{T}
is
extension-closed in
\mathcal{T}
if
\mathcal{P}=\mathcal{P}*\mathcal{P}
. One also has a notion of extension-closure for subcategories of Quillen exact categories (e.g. abelian categories), where exact sequences play the role of triangles.

An additive subcategory
\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{T}
is
suspended
(resp.
co-suspended
) if it is extension-closed and closed under the suspension functor
\Sigma
(resp. inverse suspension functor
\Sigma^{-1}
). The ideal
[\mathcal{P}]
in
\mathcal{C}
contains precisely the morphisms that factor through an object in
\mathcal{P}
. The ideal quotient will be denoted by
{\mathcal{C}\over[\mathcal{P}]}
. If
\mathcal{P}=\add(P)
for some object
P
, we denote this quotient by
{\mathcal{C}\over[P]}
.

We use Deligne’s convention, writing
F=G
when we mean that these functors are naturally isomorphic.

1.1.
t-structures and wide subcategories of the heart

Truncation structures (t-structures for short) were introduced by Beilinson–Bernstein–Deligne
[
BBD82
]
(and also Gabber
[
BBDG18
]
). We give a quick survey of their elementary properties. A triangulated category
\mathcal{D}
with suspension functor
\Sigma
is fixed.

Definition 1.1
.

A pair of full additive subcategories
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})
of
\mathcal{D}
constitute a
truncation structure
(henceforth
t-structure
) if the conditions
(t.1)
and
(t.2)
below are met.

(t.1)

(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})
is a
torsion pair
in
\mathcal{D}
, i.e.

(t.1.1)

The Hom-spaces
\mathcal{D}(X,Y)
are trivial for all
X\in\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}
and
Y\in\mathcal{D}^{>0}
,

(t.1.2)

every object in
\mathcal{D}
is an extension of an object in
\mathcal{D}^{>0}
with an object in
\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}
. This is to say that
\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}*\mathcal{D}^{>0}=\mathcal{D}
.

(t.2)

The subcategory
\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}
is suspended (equivalently, the subcategory
\mathcal{D}^{>0}
is co-suspended).

We define
\mathcal{D}^{\leq-1}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}\Sigma\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}
. More generally, we define

\displaystyle\mathcal{D}^{\leq n}

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}\Sigma^{-n}\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},

\displaystyle\mathcal{D}^{>m}

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}\Sigma^{-m}\mathcal{D}^{>0},

\displaystyle\mathcal{D}^{[m,n]}

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}\mathcal{D}^{>m-1}\cap\mathcal{D}^{\leq n},

\displaystyle\text{and }\mathcal{D}^{m}

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}\mathcal{D}^{[m,m]},

for integers
n
and
m
. The t-structure
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})
is
bounded
if
\bigcup\limits_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}\mathcal{D}^{[m,n]}=\mathcal{D}
. The subcategory
\mathcal{D}^{0}
of
\mathcal{D}
is called the
heart
of the t-structure.

Remark 1.2
.

The subcategories
\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}
and
\mathcal{D}^{>0}
determine each other; we have that
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0})^{\perp_{0}}=\mathcal{D}^{>0}
and that
{{}^{\perp_{0}}(\mathcal{D}^{>0})}=\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}
. As a result of this fact, the subcategories
\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}
and
\mathcal{D}^{>0}
are closed under taking direct summands.

Let
\mathcal{A}
be an abelian category. Then the derived category
\Der(\mathcal{A})
can be equipped with the
standard t-structure
:

\displaystyle\Der^{\leq 0}(\mathcal{A})

\displaystyle=\{X\in\Der(\mathcal{A})\,\,|\,\,\Hom_{\Der(A)}(T,X)=0\text{ for all }i>0\},

\displaystyle\Der^{>0}(\mathcal{A})

\displaystyle=\{X\in\Der(\mathcal{A})\,\,|\,\,\Hom_{\Der(A)}(T,X)=0\text{ for all }i\leq 0\}.

It restricts to a bounded t-structure on
\Der_{\rm fd}(\mathcal{A})
, also called the
standard t-structure
.
The heart of these t-structures are both equivalent to the abelian category
\mathcal{A}
. In general, the heart of any t-structure is an abelian category
[
BBD82
, Théorème 1.3.6]
.

For a suspended subcategory
\mathcal{U}\subseteq\mathcal{D}
, the pair
(\mathcal{U},\mathcal{U}^{\perp})
forms a t-structure on
\mathcal{D}
if and only if
\mathcal{U}
is
co-reflective

[
KV88
, 1.1 Proposition]
, i.e. the inclusion admits a right adjoint.
A subcategory of
\mathcal{D}
is called an
aisle
(resp. a
co-aisle
) if it is suspended (resp. co-suspended) and co-reflective (resp.
reflective
, i.e. the inclusion admits a left adjoint).
Since the pair
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})
is a t-structure on
\mathcal{D}
precisely when
\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}
is an aisle in
\mathcal{D}
(or, equivalently
\mathcal{D}^{>0}
is a co-aisle), we say that
\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}
is the
aisle of the t-structure
(and that
\mathcal{D}^{>0}
is the
co-aisle
).

truncation functor

Remark 1.3
.

It is conventional to denote the truncation functors by
\tau^{\leq 0}
and
\tau^{>0}
. We have chosen to use
\sigma^{\leq 0}
and
\sigma^{>0}
instead, so that they will not be confused with the Auslander–Reiten translation.

is

(1)

left t-exact
if
F(\mathcal{U}^{>0})\subseteq\mathcal{D}^{>0}
,

(2)

right t-exact
if
F(\mathcal{U}^{\leq 0})\subseteq\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}
,

(3)

t-exact
if it is both left t-exact and right t-exact.

A
t-exact subcategory
of
\mathcal{D}
with respect to the t-structure
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})
, is a triangulated subcategory
\mathcal{S}
of
\mathcal{D}
such that
\sigma^{\leq 0}X\in\mathcal{S}
for any
X\in\mathcal{S}
.

Remark 1.6
.

We might as well have defined a t-exact subcategory to be a triangulated subcategory which is closed under any truncation functor of the form
\sigma^{\leq i}
or
\sigma^{>i}
, not just
\sigma^{\leq 0}
. First of all, a t-exact subcategory
\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathcal{D}
is closed under truncation by
\sigma^{\leq m}
, for all
m\in\mathbb{Z}
, since we have assumed that
\mathcal{S}
is closed under suspension and desuspension.
It is also closed under
\sigma^{>0}
(and thus
\sigma^{>m}
, for all
m\in\mathbb{Z}
), which one proves by forming a truncation triangle
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma^{\leq 0}X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma^{>0}X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma\sigma^{\leq 0}X,}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varepsilon_{X}}

where
X\in\mathcal{S}
, and then pointing out that
\sigma^{>0}X
is a cone of
\varepsilon_{X}
, a morphism in the triangulated subcategory
\mathcal{S}
.

The t-exact subcategories of
\mathcal{D}
are precisely those on which we can induce a t-structure
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}\cap~\mathcal{S},\mathcal{D}^{>0}\cap~\mathcal{S})
such that the inclusion functor

}{{{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@transformcm{1.0}{0.0}{0.0}{1.0}{2.63889pt}{-1.81079pt}\lxSVG@begingroup@{transform} \pgfsys@hbox{60}\lxSVG@closescope }}}

\lxSVG@closescope {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}\hskip 0.86108pt}\mathcal{D}
be a t-exact functor. Then the composite functor
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{U}^{0}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{U}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}^{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\sigma}^{0}}

is an exact functor of abelian categories. In particular, if
\mathcal{S}
is a t-exact subcategory of
\mathcal{D}
, then
\mathcal{S}^{0}
is an exact abelian subcategory of
\mathcal{D}^{0}
.

The subcategory
\mathcal{D}^{0}=\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0}\cap\mathcal{D}^{>0}
is an intersection of extension-closed subcategories. If
\mathcal{S}
is a triangulated subcategory of
\mathcal{D}
, the intersection
\mathcal{D}^{0}\cap\mathcal{S}
is extension-closed in the triangulated category
\mathcal{D}
. It now follows from
Proposition

1.4
(
2
) that
\mathcal{S}^{0}=\mathcal{D}^{0}\cap\mathcal{S}
is extension-closed in the abelian category
\mathcal{D}^{0}
. An extension-closed exact abelian subcategory is often called a
wide subcategory
(or a
weak Serre subcategory
). Equivalently, it is a subcategory which is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions. In particular, every idempotent endomorphism admits a kernel, which is to say that the wide subcategory in question is idempotent complete. It follows that wide subcategories are closed under taking direct summands.

Lemma 1.8
.

Let
\mathcal{D}
be a triangulated category equipped with a bounded t-structure
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})
, and let
\mathcal{S}
be a t-exact subcategory of
\mathcal{D}
. Then
\mathcal{S}
is thick.

Proof.

It is to be shown that
\mathcal{S}
is closed under direct summands. Let
X,Y\in\mathcal{D}
be such that
X\oplus Y\in\mathcal{S}
. Since
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})
is bounded, only finitely many integers
i
are such that
{\sigma}^{i}(X\oplus Y)
is non-zero. We proceed by induction on the number
d
of such integers
i
.

The case
d=0
concerns only zero objects, and is therefore trivial to establish. If
d=1
, we have that
X\oplus Y\in\mathcal{S}^{i}
for some
i
. Since
\mathcal{S}^{i}
is equivalent to
\mathcal{S}^{0}
, we may assume without loss of generality that
i=0
. Having remarked above that wide subcategories are idempotent complete, it follows that the direct summand
X
of
X\oplus Y
is in the wide subcategory
\mathcal{S}^{0}
, as desired.

Assume that the statement is true whenever
d<\ell
for some
\ell\geq 2
. If
d=\ell
, suppose that
X\oplus Y\in\mathcal{S}
has non-vanishing cohomology in
\ell
positions, and let
m
be the smallest integer such that
\sigma^{>m+1}(X\oplus Y)=0
. Let
{X_{1}=\sigma^{\leq m}X}
and
{X_{2}=\sigma^{>m}X}
. In the truncation triangle

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma X_{1},}

the object
X_{1}
has non-vanishing cohomology in
\ell-1
positions, and
X_{2}
has non-vanishing cohomology in one position. In the same vein, let
Y_{1}=\sigma^{\leq m}Y
and
Y_{2}=\sigma^{>m}Y
. In the truncation triangle

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y_{1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y_{2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma Y_{1},}

the objects
Y_{1}
and
Y_{2}
have the same properties as
X_{1}
and
X_{2}
above. Then
X_{1}\oplus Y_{1}=\sigma^{\leq m}(X\oplus Y)
and
X_{2}\oplus Y_{2}=\sigma^{>m}(X\oplus Y)
are objects in
\mathcal{S}
with cohomology in fewer than
\ell
positions, whence
X_{1},X_{2}\in\mathcal{S}
by the induction hypothesis. Since
\mathcal{S}
is a triangulated subcategory of
\mathcal{D}
, it follows that
X\in\mathcal{S}
, since it is an extension of
X_{2}
in
X_{1}
.
∎

Following Zhang–Cai
[
ZC17
, Definition 2.3]
, we say that a thick subcategory
\mathcal{S}
of
\mathcal{D}
is
{\sigma}^{0}
-stable
if
{\sigma}^{0}X\in\mathcal{S}
for all
X\in\mathcal{S}
. Having defined the cohomology functor
{\sigma}^{i}
by
{\sigma}^{0}\circ\Sigma^{n}
, it is equivalent to impose that
\mathcal{S}
is closed under all cohomology functors
{\sigma}^{i}
.

Lemma 1.9
.

Let
\mathcal{D}
be a triangulated category equipped with a t-structure
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})
.
A thick subcategory
\mathcal{S}
of
\mathcal{D}
is
{\sigma}^{0}
-stable if it is t-exact. If the t-structure is bounded, the converse also holds.

Proof.

We explained in
Remark

1.6
that a t-exact subcategory
\mathcal{S}
is closed under truncation by
\sigma^{\leq 0}
and
\sigma^{>-1}
. Hence, it is closed under
{\sigma}^{0}=\sigma^{\leq 0}\sigma^{>-1}
, which is to be
{\sigma}^{0}
-stable.

Conversely, suppose that the t-structure
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})
is bounded and let
\mathcal{S}
be an
{\sigma}^{0}
-stable subcategory of
\mathcal{D}
. For any
X\in\mathcal{S}
and any integer
n
, we can form a truncation triangle
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma^{\leq n-1}X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma^{\leq n}X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-n}H^{n}X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma\sigma^{\leq n-1}X.}

The object
\Sigma^{-n}H^{n}X
lies in
\mathcal{S}
, and hence
\sigma^{\leq n-1}X
belongs to
\mathcal{S}
if and only if
\sigma^{\leq n}X
does. By induction, it follows that
\sigma^{\leq 0}X\in\mathcal{S}
if and only if
\sigma^{\leq n}X\in\mathcal{S}
, where
n
is an arbitrary integer.
The boundedness of the t-structure ensures that
\sigma^{\leq n}X=X
for some
n
; indeed, the object
X
lies in some subcategory of
\mathcal{D}
of the form
\mathcal{D}^{[m,n]}
, where the truncation functor
\sigma^{\leq n}
acts as the identity. We conclude that
\mathcal{S}
is t-exact, having shown that
\sigma^{\leq 0}X\in\mathcal{S}
for any
X\in\mathcal{S}
.
∎

Fix a t-structure
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})
on
\mathcal{D}
. The set of t-exact subcategories of
\mathcal{D}
with respect to
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})
is closed under arbitrary intersections of aisles. Ordering this set with respect to inclusion of the aisles, it has been endowed with the structure of a complete lattice. The join of a family
\{\mathcal{S}_{i}\}_{i\in I}
is the smallest t-exact subcategory containing all
\mathcal{S}_{i}
, whereas the meet is computed by intersection. We denote this lattice by
\texact_{(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})}(\mathcal{D})
, and we let
\wide(\mathcal{D}^{0})
denote the lattice of wide subcategories in
\mathcal{D}^{0}
, ordered by inclusion. We conclude this subsection with a result providing mutually inverse isomorphisms between these lattices, and a lemma that will be handy for later use.

\mathcal{S}

\mathcal{D}^{0}
.

(2)

For
\mathcal{W}\in\wide(\mathcal{D}^{0})
, let
\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{W}}
be as in
Theorem

1.10
. We have that
\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{W}}=\thick_{\mathcal{D}}(\mathcal{W})
.

Proof.

We first prove (
1
). Let
\mathcal{S}
be a t-exact subcategory of
\mathcal{D}
. For any
X\in\mathcal{S}\cap\mathcal{D}^{0}
, we have that
{\sigma}^{0}X
is isomorphic to
X
, putting
X
in
{\sigma}^{0}\mathcal{S}
, namely the essential image of
\mathcal{S}
under the cohomology functor. This shows that
\mathcal{S}\cap\mathcal{D}^{0}\subseteq{\sigma}^{0}\mathcal{S}
. The reverse inclusion
\mathcal{S}\cap\mathcal{D}^{0}\supseteq{\sigma}^{0}\mathcal{S}
also holds; we have that
{\sigma}^{0}\mathcal{S}
is contained in
\mathcal{D}^{0}
by the definition of the cohomology functor, and in
\mathcal{S}
by the
{\sigma}^{0}
-stability of
\mathcal{S}
(see
Lemma

1.9
).

Secondly and finally, we prove (
2
). We will regard the wide subcategory
\mathcal{W}\subseteq\mathcal{D}^{0}
as a subcategory of
\mathcal{D}
. Since
\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{W}}
is a thick subcategory of
\mathcal{D}
containing
\mathcal{W}
, it immediately follows that
\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{W}}\supseteq\thick_{\mathcal{D}}(\mathcal{W})
. We complete the proof by showing that any object
X\in\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{W}}
can be built from objects in
\mathcal{W}
using extensions, (de)suspensions and direct summands. Since the t-structure
(\mathcal{D}^{\leq 0},\mathcal{D}^{>0})
is bounded, there exists some interval
[m,n]
of integers such that
X\in\mathcal{D}^{[m,n]}
. We proceed by induction of the length of this interval, namely the integer
\ell=n-m
. The case
\ell=0
concerns intervals of the form
[m,m]
. We can build any object in
\mathcal{D}^{[m,m]}\cap\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{W}}
by (de)suspending objects in
\mathcal{W}
, thus settling the anchor step. Suppose that the statement has been shown for all intervals of length shorter than
\ell
, where
\ell\geq 1
. Supposing that
X\in\mathcal{D}^{[m,n]}\cap\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{W}}
, and that the interval
[m,n]
is of length
\ell
, one considers the truncation triangle
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma^{\leq n-1}X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma^{>n-1}X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma\sigma^{\leq n-1}X.}

By
Lemma

1.9
, the objects
\sigma^{\leq n-1}X
and
\sigma^{>n-1}X
are in
\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{W}}
by t-exactness.
By the induction hypothesis, both objects are in
\thick_{\mathcal{D}}(\mathcal{W})
. Since
X
is an extension of the two, we conclude that
X\in\thick_{\mathcal{D}}(\mathcal{W})
. By the Principle of Induction, we conclude that
\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{W}}\subseteq\thick_{\mathcal{D}}(\mathcal{W})
, and in turn that these triangulated subcategories of
\mathcal{D}
are equal.
∎

1.2.
Silting and
\tau
-tilting

Definition 1.12
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a triangulated category with suspension functor
\Sigma
. An object
{X}\in\mathcal{C}
is
presilting
if
\mathcal{C}({X},\Sigma^{n}{X})=0
for all positive integers
n
. A presilting object
{X}
is a
silting object
if, in addition,
\thick({X})=\mathcal{C}
.

Recall that if
\mathcal{C}
is a Krull–Schmidt
k
-category, an object
X\in\mathcal{C}
is
basic
if any two distinct indecomposable direct summands of
X
are non-isomorphic.
The sets of basic presilting and basic silting objects in
\mathcal{C}
are denoted by
\mathrm{presilt}(\mathcal{C})
and
\mathrm{silt}(\mathcal{C})
, respectively.
The subsets containing the objects having a fixed (basic) presilting object
{P}
as a direct summand are denoted by
\mathrm{presilt}_{P}(\mathcal{C})
and
\mathrm{silt}_{P}(\mathcal{C})
, respectively.

Definition 1.13
.

For a fixed silting object
{S}\in\mathcal{C}
, we say that an object
{P}\in\mathcal{C}

2_{S}
-term

where
{S}_{1},{S}_{0}\in\add({S})
.
The set of basic
2_{S}
-term presilting objects is denoted by
2_{S}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(\mathcal{C})
, and the subset of basic
2_{S}
-term silting objects by
2_{S}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{silt}(\mathcal{C})
. The subsets containing those having a (basic) presilting object
{P}
is a direct summand are denoted by
2_{S}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}_{P}(\mathcal{C})
and
2_{S}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{silt}_{P}(\mathcal{C})
, respectively. When the choice of silting object
S
is clear from context, we refer to
2_{S}
-term (pre)silting objects as
two-term (pre)silting objects
.

We note that
S
in the above definition does not have to be basic. However, if
R
denotes the largest basic direct summand of
S
, the set of basic
2_{S}
-term silting objects in
\mathcal{C}
coincides with that of basic
2_{R}
-term silting objects in
\mathcal{C}
. Thanks to this fact, we will not need to assume that
S
is basic in our results.

If
\mathcal{C}=\Kb(\proj{\Lambda})
, the bounded homotopy category of a finite dimensional
k
-algebra
{\Lambda}
, then
{\Lambda}
is a silting object in
\mathcal{C}
(removing redundant direct summands will yield a basic silting object). More generally, if
A
is a non-positive dg
k
-algebra, then
A
is silting in
\per(A)
.
In these cases, we write
2\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{silt}(A)
for the set of
2_{A}
-term basic silting objects in
\per(A)
(and so on), omitting the subscript beneath the symbol
2
.

The set
2_{S}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{silt}(\mathcal{C})
admits a partial order
\geq
, where
{P}\geq{Q}
provided that
\mathcal{C}({P},\Sigma^{n}{Q})=0
whenever
n>0

[
AI12
, Theorem 2.11 and Proposition 2.14]
.
If
\mathcal{C}
is Hom-finite and Krull–Schmidt, it turns out that any
2_{S}
-term presilting object
{P}\in\mathcal{C}
can be completed to a
2_{S}
-term silting object. One such silting object is the
Bongartz completion

{T^{+}_{P}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}{P}\oplus{Q^{+}}
of
{P}
, where
{Q^{+}}
is defined by the triangle

There is a close connection between the
2_{S}
-term silting theory of
\mathcal{C}
and the support
\tau
-tilting theory of the finite dimensional
k
-algebra
\End_{\mathcal{C}}({S})
. We now recall the definitions and results of
\tau
-tilting theory
[
AIR14
]
.

Definition 1.14
.

For a finite dimensional
k
-algebra
{\Lambda}
, a finitely generated right
{\Lambda}
-module
M
is
\tau
-rigid
if
\Hom_{{\Lambda}}(M,\tau M)=0
, where
\tau
is the Auslander–Reiten translation. A pair
(M,Q)
is
\tau
-rigid
if
M
is a
\tau
-rigid module and
Q
is a finitely generated projective right
{\Lambda}
-module such that
\Hom_{{\Lambda}}(Q,M)=0
. A
\tau
-rigid pair
(M,Q)
is
support
\tau
-tilting
if
|M|+|Q|=|{\Lambda}|
, where
|X|
is the number of non-isomorphic indecomposable direct summands of
X
. An
{\Lambda}
-module
M
is
support
\tau
-tilting
if there exists a projective
{\Lambda}
-module
Q
such that
(M,Q)
is a support
\tau
-tilting pair.

We identify the
\tau
-rigid pairs
(M,Q)
and
(N,R)
if
\add(M)=\add(N)
and
\add(Q)=\add(R)
. We say that
(M,Q)
is
basic
if no two indecomposable direct summands of
(M,Q)
are isomorphic. By the Krull–Schmidt property of
\fgMod{{\Lambda}}
, any
\tau
-rigid pair can be identified with a basic
\tau
-rigid pair.
A
\tau
-rigid pair
(N,R)
is a
direct summand
of the
\tau
-rigid pair
(M,Q)
if
N
is a direct summand of
M
and
R
is a direct summand of
Q
. Note that indecomposable
\tau
-rigid pairs necessarily have the zero module as exactly one of the two components. If
(M,Q)
and
(M,R)
are support
\tau
-tilting pairs, then
\add(Q)=\add(R)

[
AIR14
, Proposition 2.3(b)]
, so
Q=R
if these pairs are basic. It follows that we have a one-to-one correspondence between basic support
\tau
-tilting modules and basic support
\tau
-tilting pairs, which truncates a pair
(M,Q)
to
M
.

We denote the set of basic
\tau
-rigid pairs in
\fgMod{\Lambda}
by
\staurigidpair({\Lambda})
, and those having a
\tau
-rigid pair
(M,Q)
as a direct summand by
\staurigidpair_{(M,Q)}({\Lambda})
. Both of these sets contain subsets consisting of basic support
\tau
-tilting pairs, that are denoted by
\stautiltpair({\Lambda})
and
\stautiltpair_{(M,Q)}({\Lambda})
, respectively. Also, let
\stautilt(\Lambda)
denote the set of basic support
\tau
-tilting
\Lambda
-modules up to isomorphism. We say that a
k
-algebra is
\tau
-tilting finite
if
\stautilt(\Lambda)
is a finite set.

The set of support
\tau
-tilting
{\Lambda}
-modules is inextricably linked with functorially finite torsion classes of
\fgMod{\Lambda}
. Recall that a
torsion class
(resp.

torsion-free class
) of
\fgMod{\Lambda}
is a subcategory which is closed under factor modules (resp. submodules) and extensions. If
\mathcal{G}
is a torsion class, the right perpendicular category
\mathcal{G}^{\perp}
is a torsion-free class. Dually, the left perpendicular category of a torsion-free class is a torsion class. A
torsion pair
is a pair of subcategories
(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{F})
where
\mathcal{G}^{\perp}=\mathcal{F}
and
{{}^{\perp}\mathcal{F}}=\mathcal{G}
. It is indeed the case that
\mathcal{G}
is a torsion class and that
\mathcal{F}
is a torsion-free class. For every
X\in\fgMod{\Lambda}
one has a canonical exact sequence

Since the set of torsion classes is partially ordered under inclusion, this bijection induces a partial order on
\stautilt({\Lambda})
and
\stautiltpair({\Lambda})
. More explicitly, we impose that
M\geq N
if
\gen(M)\supseteq\gen(N)
. If
(M,Q)
and
(N,R)
are basic support

2.
Silting t-structures and reduction

Silting reduction is a well-developed reduction technique, particularly for Hom-finite Krull–Schmidt triangulated categories
[
IY18
]
. The bijections in question restrict to two-term objects and are compatible with
\tau
-tilting reduction
[
Jas15
, Theorem 4.12]
. In this section, we study the interplay between silting reduction and t-structures. Iyama–Yang prove the following theorem, though in greater generality.

Theorem 2.1

(
[
IY18
, Theorems 3.1, 3.6, and 3.7]
,
[
Jas15
, Proposition 4.11]
)
.

Lemma 2.4
.

Let
{P}\oplus{Q}
be a basic
2_{S}
-term presilting object in
\mathcal{C}
. Then the diagram

(2.E)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 2_{S}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}(\mathcal{C})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 2_{T^{+}_{P}}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}_{\varphi_{P}({P\oplus}Q)}(\mathcal{Z}_{P}/[{P}])}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 2_{T^{+}_{Q}}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}_{\varphi_{Q}(P{\oplus Q})}(\mathcal{Z}_{Q}/[{Q}])}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 2_{{T}^{+}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}/[{P}\oplus{Q}])}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{Q}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{P}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{{P}\oplus{Q}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{\varphi_{P}({Q})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{\varphi_{Q}({P})}}

commutes.

Proof.

For the sake of terseness, let
[Q]
denote the ideal of
\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}/[{P}]
consisting of morphisms factoring through
\add(Q)
, and similarly for the ideal
[P]
of
\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}/[{Q}]
. By the Third Isomorphism Theorem, we have additive equivalences

(2.F)

{\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}/[{P}]\over[{Q}]}\simeq{\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}/[{P}]\over[{P}\oplus{Q}]/[{P}]}\simeq{\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}\over[{P}\oplus{Q}]},

and similarly

(2.G)

{\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}/[{Q}]\over[{P}]}\simeq{\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}\over[{P}\oplus{Q}]}.

The isomorphisms in (
2.F
) and (
2.G
) enable the construction of an essentially commutative diagram of ideal quotient functors

(2.H)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}/[{P}]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}/[{Q}]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}/[{P}\oplus{Q}]}

Theorem

2.1
(
2
) asserts that the functors going out of
\mathcal{Z}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}
induce the bijections going out of
2_{S}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}_{{P}\oplus{Q}}(\mathcal{C})
in (
2.E
).

We complete the proof by showing that the maps
\varphi_{\varphi_{Q}(P\oplus Q)}
and
\varphi_{\varphi_{P}(P\oplus Q)}
have the claimed codomain, and that they factorise
\varphi_{P\oplus Q}
as shown in (
2.E
).
To give an argument as to why
\varphi_{\varphi_{Q}(P\oplus Q)}
(and similarly
\varphi_{\varphi_{P}(P\oplus Q)}
) has the claimed codomain in (
2.E
), it suffices to show that the functor on the bottom of (
2.H
) has the following property:

We will now state our setup, for the sake of future reference.

Setup 2.5
.

Let
A
be a non-positive dg
k
-algebra such that
H^{i}A
is finite dimensional for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
, and let
P
be a basic two-term presilting object in
\per(A)
, i.e. an object in
2\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(A)
.

We are requiring
H^{i}A
to be finite dimensional for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
so that
\per(A)
becomes Hom-finite
[
Ami09
, Proof of Proposition 2.4]
(and consequently Krull–Schmidt, by idempotent completeness).
Note that finite dimensional
k
-algebras are included in our setup.
It would be possible to generalise
2.5
to the setting of ST-triples
(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D},S)

[
AMY19
, §4]
. We do not give the definition of ST-triples here, but we note that if
\mathcal{C}
is an algebraic triangulated category (i.e. triangle equivalent to the stable category of a Frobenius category), this triple is equivalent to a triple of the form
(\per(A),\Der_{\rm fd}(A),A)
, where
A
is as in
2.5

[
AMY19
, Proposition 6.12]
. The assumption of algebricity does not reduce the scope of applications at time of writing; the use of ST-triples seems not to have occurred in a non-algebraic context.

In this section, we describe Iyama–Yang silting reduction and its interaction with silting t-structures. Silting reduction with respect to
P
occurs in the Verdier quotient
\per(A)/\thick(P)
, but we will show that subcategory

P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{\rm fd}{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}}P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}\cap\Der_{\rm fd}(A)
of
\Der_{\rm fd}(A)
also plays a role, where
P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}
is a right perpendicular subcategory of
\Der(A)
(see (
1.A
)). If
\per(A)/\thick(P)
is triangle equivalent to
\per(C)
for some dg algebra
C
, then
P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
is triangle equivalent to
\Der_{\rm fd}(C)
(see
Corollary

2.11
). Note that
P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
is a thick subcategory of
\Der_{\rm fd}(A)
. The t-structures defined by these silting objects will be restricted to
P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
, which is achievable since
P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
is a t-exact subcategory of
\Der_{\rm fd}(A)
(see
Proposition

2.8
).

We first specify what it means for a t-structure to be generated by a silting object. We employ the following notational convention: Given an object
T
in
\per(A)
and
I\subseteq\mathbb{Z}
, let
T^{\perp_{I}}
denote the right perpendicular of
\Der(A)
, as defined in (
1.A
), and define
T^{\perp_{I}}_{\rm fd}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}T^{\perp_{I}}\cap\Der_{\rm fd}(A)
.

Proposition-Definition 2.6

(
[
AMY19
, Proposition 4.6]
)
.

Let
T
be a silting object in
\per(A)
.
The pair
(T^{\perp_{>0}},T^{\perp_{\leq 0}})
forms a t-structure on
\Der(A)
. It restricts to a t-structure
(T^{\perp_{>0}}_{\rm fd},T^{\perp_{\leq 0}}_{\rm fd})
on
\Der_{\rm fd}(A)
. A t-structure of one of these forms is said to be a
silting t-structure
, and it is
generated
by
T
.

{\sigma}^{0}_{T}

Lemma 2.7
.

Let
A
and
P
be as in
2.5
and let
(\mathcal{U},\mathcal{U}^{\perp_{{0}}})
be a t-structure on
\Der_{\rm fd}(A)
such that
\mathcal{U}\subseteq P^{\perp_{>1}}_{{\rm fd}}
and
\mathcal{U}^{\perp_{{0}}}\subseteq P^{\perp_{\leq 0}}_{\rm fd}
. Then the subcategory
P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
is t-exact with respect to
(\mathcal{U},\mathcal{U}^{\perp_{{0}}})
. In particular, the pair
(\mathcal{U}\cap P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}},\mathcal{U}^{\perp_{{0}}}\cap P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}})
is a t-structure on
P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
.

Proof.

Let
\sigma_{\mathcal{U}}
and
\sigma_{\mathcal{U}^{\perp_{{0}}}}
be the truncation functors for
(\mathcal{U},\mathcal{U}^{\perp_{{0}}})
. Fixing an arbitrary object
X\in P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
, it suffices to show that
\sigma_{\mathcal{U}}X\in P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
. We have a truncation triangle

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma_{\mathcal{U}}X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma_{\mathcal{U}^{\perp_{{0}}}}X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma\sigma_{\mathcal{U}}X.}

Since
\sigma_{\mathcal{U}^{\perp_{{0}}}}X\in\mathcal{U}^{\perp_{{0}}}\subseteq P^{\perp_{\leq 0}}_{{\rm fd}}
, the desuspension
\Sigma^{-1}\sigma_{\mathcal{U}^{\perp_{{0}}}}X
is in
P^{\perp_{\leq 1}}_{{\rm fd}}
. Using that
P^{\perp_{\leq 1}}_{{\rm fd}}
is extension-closed in
\Der_{\rm fd}(A)
, we deduce that
\sigma_{\mathcal{U}}X\in P^{\perp_{\leq 1}}_{{\rm fd}}
. Since
\sigma_{\mathcal{U}}X
also belongs to
\mathcal{U}
, and thus to
P^{\perp_{>1}}_{{\rm fd}}
, it follows that
\sigma_{\mathcal{U}}X\in P^{\perp_{\leq 1}}_{{\rm fd}}\cap P^{\perp_{>1}}_{{\rm fd}}=P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
, as desired.
∎

Proposition 2.8
.

Let
A
be as in
2.5
.

(1)

Let
T
be a silting object in
\per(A)
of which
Q
is a direct summand. Then
Q^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
is t-exact with respect to the t-structure
(T^{\perp_{>0}}_{{\rm fd}},T^{\perp_{\leq 0}}_{{\rm fd}})
on
\Der_{\rm fd}(A)
.

(2)

Let
P\in 2\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(A)
(as in
2.5
). Then
P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
is t-exact with respect to the standard t-structure
(A^{\perp_{>0}}_{{\rm fd}},A^{\perp_{\leq 0}}_{{\rm fd}})
on
\Der_{\rm fd}(A)
.

Proof.

We will prove that both assertions are consequences of
Lemma

2.7
.

We first address (
1
). It is clear that
T^{\perp_{>0}}_{{\rm fd}}\subseteq Q^{\perp_{>0}}_{{\rm fd}}\subseteq Q^{\perp_{>1}}_{{\rm fd}}
and
T^{\perp_{\leq 0}}_{{\rm fd}}\subseteq Q^{\perp_{\leq 0}}_{\rm fd}
, since
Q
is a direct summand of
T
.

We move on to (
2
).

P

.

Proof.

We first prove (
1
).
By

1.11
(
2
), the bijection
-\cap A^{\perp_{\neq 0}}_{\rm fd}
in (
2.J
) is inverted by
\thick_{\Der_{\rm fd}(A)}(-)
. Since these are mutually inverse isomorphisms of posets, it suffices to prove that

(2.L)

\displaystyle P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}\cap A^{\perp_{\neq 0}}_{{\rm fd}}

\displaystyle\subseteq{I(M,Q)},

(2.M)

\displaystyle\thick_{\Der_{\rm fd}(A)}\big({I(M,Q)}\big)

\displaystyle\subseteq P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}.

where
I(M,Q)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}{M^{\perp_{0}}\cap{{}^{\perp_{0}}(\tau M)}\cap Q^{\perp_{0}}\cap A^{\perp_{\neq 0}}_{\rm fd}}\subseteq A^{\perp_{\neq 0}}
.

The inclusion in (
2.L
) will be addressed first. Let
X\in P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}\cap A^{\perp_{\neq 0}}_{{\rm fd}}
. It is to be deduced that
X\in M^{\perp_{0}}\,\cap\,{{}^{\perp_{0}}(\tau M)\cap Q^{\perp_{0}}}
. The assertion that
X\in Q^{\perp_{0}}
is immediate, having assumed that
X\in P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}\subseteq Q^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
.
Consider the following truncation triangle in the t-structure
(A^{\perp_{\geq 0}},A^{\perp_{<0}})
on
\Der(A)
(the once suspension of the standard one):

(2.N)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma^{<0}_{A}P}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\sigma^{\geq 0}_{A}P}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma\sigma^{<0}_{A}P}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
\simeq

Since
P
is two-term (so
\sigma^{\geq 1}P\simeq 0
) and
{\sigma}^{0}_{A}P\simeq M
, the third term in this triangle is indeed isomorphic to
M
.
The outer terms in (
2.N
) are in
A^{\perp_{\geq 0}}
, so there are no non-trivial maps from these objects to
X\in A^{\perp_{\neq 0}}_{\rm fd}\subseteq A^{\perp_{<0}}_{\rm fd}
. Applying the contravariant functor
\Hom_{\Der(A)}(-,X)
to the triangle in (
2.N
) thus yields an isomorphism

(2.O)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Hom_{\Der(A)}(P,X)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Hom_{\Der(A)}(M,X),}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

so
X\in M^{\perp_{0}}
.

\Hom_{H^{0}A}(X,\tau M)=0

P
into
P_{M}\oplus\Sigma Q

in
\Sigma A

\Der(A)

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p_{M}}

P_{0},P_{1}\in\proj(A)
and
p_{M}
is a right minimal morphism. By
2.6

(2.P)

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p_{M}\circ-}

is readily checked to be a minimal projective presentation of the

Section

4
is devoted to the construction of the
\tau
-cluster morphism category in terms of two-term silting. We conclude this section with results that will turn out useful for this purpose. To prove them, we will apply some basic results from the localisation theory of compactly generated triangulated categories, especially in the “large” derived category
\Der(A)
, where the objects are possibly unbounded complexes of possibly infinitely generated modules.
Proposition

2.10
addresses the localisation theory we need, whereas the subsequent corollaries will be applied in later sections.

Proof.

The assertion in (
1
) is taken directly from the cited reference. We note that
\Loc(P)^{\perp_{0}}=P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}
; the left hand side is contained in the right hand side since
\Loc(P)\supseteq P[i]
for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
, and the right hand side is contained in the left since
\Loc(P)
can be built from
\add(P)
using suspensions, desuspensions, extensions, and coproducts. The functors
\iota_{P}
and
\lambda_{P}
are naturally isomorphic to the inclusion functors, and we will simply treat them as inclusions for the remainder of this proof.

Assertion (
2
) now easily follows from (
1
), as we now show.
Recall that the Bongartz completion
T^{+}_{P}
is given by
P\oplus Q^{+}
, where
Q^{+}
is defined by the triangle (see (
1.C
))

(2.S)

This last functor can be obtained by restricting the equivalence in (
2.T
) to compact objects. It is thus an equivalence, thanks to the idempotent completeness of
\Der(C_{P})

[
Nee92
, Theorem 2.1]
. This proves (
4
).

Right adjoints between derived categories of dg algebras preserve boundedness if the left adjoint preserves compactness
[
GP18
, Lemma 4.2]
. Since
{\varpi_{P}}
preserves compactness, the last assertion (
5
) now follows from (
4
).
∎

Corollary 2.11
.

Let
A
and
P
be as in
2.5
, and let
C_{P}
as in
Proposition

2.10
(
3
).
Then there is a triangle equivalence
P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}\simeq\Der_{\mathrm{fd}}(C_{P})
.

Proof.

Proposition

2.10
(
3
) provides an equivalence from the perpendicular subcategory
P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}
of
\Der(A)
to
\Der(C_{P})
, sending
{\varpi_{P}}A
to
C_{P}
. In order to prove that this equivalence restricts to the bounded derived categories, it remains to show that the vector space
\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}\Hom_{\Der(A)}(A,\Sigma^{i}\iota_{P}X)
is finite dimensional precisely when
\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}\Hom_{P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}}(\varpi_{P}A,\Sigma^{i}X)
is finite dimensional, where
X\in P^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}
, but this follows directly from
Proposition

2.10
(
1
), or more specifically the fact that
({\varpi_{P}},\iota_{P})
is an adjoint pair of triangle functors.∎

3.
Compatibility of the Iyama–Yang and Buan–Marsh bijections

Reduction techniques have been developed for both silting objects (known as
silting reduction

[
IY18
]
) and support
\tau
-tilting modules (
\tau
-tilting reduction

[
Jas15
]
), and they are compatible
[
Jas15
, Theorem 4.12(b)]
. In this section we generalise Jasso’s compatibility theorem, by showing that the support
\tau
-tilting reduction of Buan–Marsh
[
BM21
, Section 3]
is compatible with silting reduction.

)

Case I(b):
If
{N}
is an indecomposable
{\Lambda}
-module such that
M\oplus{N}
is
\tau
-rigid and
{N}\in\gen(M)
, define
\mathcal{E}_{(M,0)}({M\oplus}{N},0)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}\big(0,f_{M}{H^{0}P_{{N}}\langle-1\rangle}\big)
, where

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{P_{{N}}\langle-1\rangle}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({{P}_{M}})_{{N}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{P}_{{N}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma P_{{N}}\langle-1\rangle}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{{P}_{{N}}}}

is a distinguished triangle in
\Kb(\proj\Lambda)
and
\beta_{{P}_{{N}}}
is a minimal right
\add({P}_{M})
-approximation.

Case I(c):
If
R
is an indecomposable projective
\Lambda
-module such that
\Hom_{{\Lambda}}(R,M)=0
, define

\mathcal{E}_{(M,0)}({M},R)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}\big(0,f_{M}{{H^{0}\big((\Sigma R)}\langle-1\rangle\big)}\big),

where

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{({\Sigma R})\langle-1\rangle}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({P}_{M})_{\Sigma R}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma R}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma({\Sigma R})\langle-1\rangle}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{\Sigma R}}

is a distinguished triangle in
\Kb(\proj\Lambda)
and
\beta_{\Sigma{R}}
is a minimal right
\add({P}_{M})
-approximation. Note that the last term in this triangle need not be isomorphic to
{\Sigma^{2}R}\langle-1\rangle
; we have chosen our notation to be consistent with (
2.A
).

Case II:
Suppose that
M=0
. We define
\mathcal{E}_{(0,Q)}(0,Q)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}(0,0)
.

Case II(a):
If
{{N}}
is an indecomposable
\tau
-rigid
\Lambda
-module such that
\Hom_{{\Lambda}}(Q,{{N}})=0
, define

\mathcal{E}_{(0,Q)}({{N}},{Q})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}({{N}},0).

Case II(b):
If
R
is an indecomposable projective
\Lambda
-module such that
(0,R)\in\ind_{(0,Q)}\staurigidpair({\Lambda})
, define
\mathcal{E}_{(0,Q)}(0,{Q\oplus}R)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}(0,f_{Q}(R))
.

In general:
Let
(M,Q)
be a
\tau
-rigid pair in
\fgMod{\Lambda}
. Let
(M^{{b}},0)
be the Bongartz completion of
(M,0)
and
(M^{+},0)
be the Bongartz completion of
(M,Q)
. Let
{\Gamma^{\prime}=\End(M^{b})/[M]}
be the
\tau
-tilting reduction of
{\Lambda}
with respect to
(M,0)
and
{\Gamma=\End(M^{+})/[M]}
the
\tau
-tilting reduction of
{\Lambda}
with respect to
(M,Q)
.

(N_{1},R_{1})
and
(N_{2},R_{2})
are elements in the domain such that
\gen(N_{1})\supseteq\gen(N_{2})
, one checks that
\gen(\mathcal{E}_{(M,0)}N_{1})\supseteq\gen(\mathcal{E}_{(M,0)}N_{2})
. This is a trivial matter for cases I(b) and I(c), and for I(a) this follows from the fact that the torsion-free functor
f_{M}
preserves epimorphisms.

\mathcal{E}_{(M,Q)}(X,R)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}F^{-1}_{(M,Q)}\circ F^{{\Gamma^{\prime}}}_{(0,Q^{\prime})}\circ\mathcal{E}^{{\Gamma^{\prime}}}_{(0,Q^{\prime})}\circ{F_{(M,0)}\circ\mathcal{E}_{(M,0)}},

as displayed on the right in (
3.D
) below.

(3.D)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\staurigidpair_{(M,Q)}({\Lambda})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\staurigidpair_{(0,{\widetilde{Q}})}J(M,0)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\staurigidpair_{(0,Q^{\prime})}({{\Gamma^{\prime}}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\staurigidpair J_{{\Gamma^{\prime}}}(0,Q^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\staurigidpair({\Gamma})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\staurigidpair J(M,Q)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{E}_{(M,0)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{E}_{(M,Q)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{(M,0)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{E}^{{\Gamma^{\prime}}}_{(0,Q^{\prime})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{{\Gamma^{\prime}}}_{(0,Q^{\prime})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{-1}_{(M,Q)}}

This concludes our recollection of Buan–Marsh’s bijection
\mathcal{E}_{(M,Q)}
.

Our aim is to link
\mathcal{E}_{(M,Q)}
to Iyama–Yang silting reduction. This is achievable in the following setup.

Setup 3.2
.

A Hom-finite Krull–Schmidt triangulated category
\mathcal{C}
is fixed, as well as a silting object
S\in\mathcal{C}
. Let basic
{P}
be a

-term presilting object in
\mathcal{C}
, let
{\Lambda}
denote the endomorphism algebra
\End_{\mathcal{C}}({S})
, and let
\Gamma=\End_{\mathcal{Z}_{P}/{[P]}}(T^{+}_{P})
, where

is the Bongartz completion of
P
.

Recall that
\Gamma
is isomorphic to the
\tau
-tilting reduction of the
\tau
-rigid pair

in
\fgMod\Lambda

[
Jas15
, Theorem 4.12(a)]
, where
H_{A}
is as defined in
Theorem

1.17
. This fact will be used implicitly in our proofs below.
In order to establish the compatibility of the two reduction techniques described above, we prove two important lemmas.

Lemma 3.4
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
,
{S}
,
{P}
,
{\Lambda}
, and
{\Gamma}
be as in
3.2
. Let
(M,Q)=H_{S}({P})
(where
H_{S}
is as defined in
Theorem

1.17
). Consider the equivalence
H^{\prime}_{S}
defined as the composite

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Big({\add({T^{+}_{P}})*\add({T^{+}_{P}}){\langle 1\rangle}\Big)/[{T^{+}_{P}}\langle 1\rangle]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\fgMod{\Gamma}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces J(H_{S}({P})),}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{Z}_{P}/{[P]}}
\subseteq
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{Z}_{P}\over[P]}(T^{+}_{P},-)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{H_{S}({P})}^{-1}}

(see
Theorem

1.16
and
1.19
.).
Then the resulting composite bijection

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 2_{T^{+}_{P}}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(\mathcal{Z}_{P}/{[P]})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\staurigidpair{\Gamma}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\staurigidpair J(H_{S}({P}))}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H_{T^{+}_{P}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{H_{S}({P})}^{-1}}

(see
Theorem

1.17
and (
1.F
)) can be expressed as follows:

(3.F)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{2_{T^{+}_{P}}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(\mathcal{Z}_{P}/[{P}])}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\staurigidpair J(H_{S}({P}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{\left(f_{\mathcal{C}({S},{P})}\mathcal{C}({S},{Y}),f_{\mathcal{C}({S},{P})}\mathcal{C}({S},{Y}_{1}\langle-1\rangle)\right)}.}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H^{\prime}_{S}}
\in
\in

where
{Y}_{1}
is the largest direct summand of
{Y}
in
{T^{+}_{P}}\langle 1\rangle
, and
\langle 1\rangle
is defined dually to (
2.A
).

Proof.

Fixing
Y\in 2_{T^{+}_{P}}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(\mathcal{Z}_{P}/{[P]})
, we first show that the
{\Gamma}
-module
F_{H_{S}{(P)}}f_{\mathcal{C}({S},{P})}\mathcal{C}({S},{Y})
is isomorphic to
{\mathcal{C}\over[P]}(T^{+}_{P},Y)
, yielding the claimed re-expression of the first component. In order to use the definition of
F_{H_{S}{(P)}}
provided in
1.19
, we note that if
(M^{+},Q)
is the Bongartz completion of
H_{S}{(P)}
, then
M^{+}\simeq\mathcal{C}(S,T^{+}_{P})
.
We get

F_{H_{S}{(P)}}f_{\mathcal{C}({S},{P})}\mathcal{C}({S},{Y})=\Hom_{{\Lambda}}\Big(\mathcal{C}(S,T^{+}_{P}),f_{\mathcal{C}({S},{P})}\mathcal{C}({S},{Y}))\Big).

A result of Jasso
[
Jas15
, Proposition 4.15]
proves that the right hand side is isomorphic to
{\mathcal{C}\over[P]}(T^{+}_{P},{Y})
. Since we have arrived where we desired, we conclude that the first component can be expressed as claimed.

It follows from the definition of
\langle-1\rangle
in (
2.A
) that
Y_{1}\langle-1\rangle\in 2_{T^{+}_{P}}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(\mathcal{Z}_{P}/[P])
. One obtains an expression for the second component by repeating the reasoning in the previous paragraph, replacing
Y
with
Y_{1}\langle-1\rangle
. Thus, the second component also is as claimed, and the proof is complete. ∎

We now have all ingredients to prove the main theorem of this section.

Theorem 3.5
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
,
{S}
,
P
,
{\Lambda}
, and
{\Gamma}
be as in
3.2
.
We have a commutative diagram of bijections
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 2_{S}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}_{{P}}(\mathcal{C})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\staurigidpair_{H_{S}({P})}({\Lambda})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 2_{T^{+}_{P}}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(\mathcal{Z}_{P}/[{P}])}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\staurigidpair({\Gamma})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\staurigidpair J(H_{S}({P}))}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H_{{S}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{P}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{H_{S}({P})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{E}_{H_{S}({P})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H_{T^{+}_{P}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H^{\prime}_{S}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{{H_{S}}({P})}}

where
\psi_{H_{S}({P})}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{\mbox{\scriptsize{def}}}}}{{\,=\,}}F_{{H_{S}}({P})}\circ\mathcal{E}_{H_{S}({P})}
.

Proof.

The commutativity of the lower triangle was shown in
Lemma

3.4
, and the right triangle (with
\psi_{H_{S}({P})}
along the diagonal) commutes by definition. What remains is proving that

(3.G)

H^{\prime}_{S}\circ\varphi_{P}({X})=\mathcal{E}_{H_{S}({P})}\circ H_{S}({X}),

which should hold for all
{X}\in 2_{S}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}_{{P}}(\mathcal{C})
. All maps in question are constructed to distribute over direct sums, whence it suffices to consider the case where
{X}
is of the form
P\oplus X^{\prime}
for some indecomposable object
X^{\prime}
which is not in
\add(P)
. We treat five cases, and a general case, corresponding to the definition of
\mathcal{E}_{H_{S}({P})}
we reviewed in the discussion following
Theorem

3.1
. We note that
\varphi_{P}(X)=X^{\prime}
in
\mathcal{Z}_{P}/[P]
.

Case I:
Suppose that
{P}
has no non-zero direct summands in
\Sigma{S}
.

Case I(a)
. Suppose that
{X^{\prime}}\in 2_{S}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}_{P}(\mathcal{C})
has no non-zero direct summand in
\Sigma{S}
and
\mathcal{C}({S},{X^{\prime}})\not\in\gen(\mathcal{C}({S},{P}))
. Using the definitions of
H_{S}
and
\mathcal{E}_{H_{S}({P})}
, the right hand side of (
3.G
) becomes

\mathcal{E}_{H_{S}({P})}\circ H_{S}({X})=\mathcal{E}_{H_{S}({P})}(\mathcal{C}(S,X),0)=\big({f_{\mathcal{C}(S,P)}}\mathcal{C}(S,X^{\prime}),0\big).

Using
Lemma

3.4
and that
\varphi_{P}(X)=X^{\prime}
in
\mathcal{Z}_{P}/[P]
, we re-express the left hand side of (
3.G
) as follows:

{H^{\prime}_{S}\circ\varphi_{P}({X})=\big({f_{\mathcal{C}(S,P)}}\mathcal{C}(S,X^{\prime}),{f_{\mathcal{C}(S,P)}}\mathcal{C}(S,X^{\prime}_{1}\langle-1\rangle)\big)},

where
X^{\prime}_{1}
is the largest direct summand of
X^{\prime}
in
T_{P}^{+}\langle 1\rangle
, considered as an object in
\mathcal{Z}_{P}/[P]
.
It now suffices to show that
{f_{\mathcal{C}(S,P)}}\mathcal{C}(S,X^{\prime}_{1})=0
, or indeed that
{f_{\mathcal{C}(S,P)}}\mathcal{C}(S,T_{P}^{+}\langle 1\rangle)=0
. By
Lemma

3.3
, one can proceed by showing that

Case I(b):
When addressing the present case, as well as I(c) and II(b), we will use the equality obtained in (

{H^{\prime}_{S}\circ\varphi_{P}({X})={\left(f_{\mathcal{C}({S},{P})}\mathcal{C}({S},{X^{\prime}}),f_{\mathcal{C}({S},{P})}\mathcal{C}({S},X^{\prime}_{1}\langle-1\rangle)\right)}=(0,f_{\mathcal{C}({S},{P})}\mathcal{C}({S},{X^{\prime}_{1}\langle-1\rangle})),}

Case II:

7
commutes thanks to the definition of
H^{\prime}_{S}
in
Lemma

3.4
.

The proof is complete.
∎

We have accomplished the task of linking the Buan–Marsh bijection to that of Iyama–Yang.

4.
\tau
-cluster morphism categories

We are now ready to give a generalisation of
\tau
-cluster morphism categories. In this section, let

as in
2.5
, i.e. a non-positive dg

-algebra such that

is finite dimensional for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.

(

) that the perpendicular category

. The
\tau
-cluster morphism category should keep track of this information.

We include a lemma to show that our composition rule is well-defined.

Lemma 4.2
.

Consider the diagram in (
4.E
), where
\mathcal{S}_{1}=U^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
for some
U\in 2\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(A)
, and
Q\in 2_{C_{V}}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}
, where
V
is the element
\pi_{U}^{-1}(P)
of
2\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(C_{U})
. The following assertions hold.

(1)

\pi^{-1}_{P}(Q)\in 2\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}_{P}(C_{U})
,

(2)

\mathcal{S}_{3}=\big(\pi_{U}^{-1}(Q\circ P)\big)^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
.

Proof.

The first assertion (
1
) follows directly from the existence of the bijection in (
4.F
).

Secondly and finally, we prove the claim in (
2
). By definition, we have that
\mathcal{S}_{3}=(\pi_{V}^{-1}(Q))^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
. We show that
\big(\pi_{U}^{-1}(Q\circ P)\big)^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}
is equal to
\mathcal{S}_{3}
as a t-exact subcategory of
\Der_{\mathrm{fd}}(A)
. Direct calculation shows the following:

\big(\pi_{U}^{-1}(Q\circ P)\big)^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}=\big(\pi_{U}^{-1}\pi_{P}^{-1}(Q)\big)^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}=\big(\pi_{\pi^{-1}_{U}(P)}^{-1}(Q)\big)^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}=\big(\pi_{V}^{-1}(Q)\big)^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{{\rm fd}}=\mathcal{S}_{3},

where we have used
Corollary

2.13
to get the second equality. The proof is complete.
∎

Having defined its objects, morphisms, and composition rule, we now check that
\tcmc_{A}
is a category. It is clear that the two-term presilting object
P=0
in
2\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(C_{U})
is the identity morphism on
{U^{\perp_{\mathbb{Z}}}_{\rm fd}}
. However, it is not obvious that the composition rule is associative. Buan–Marsh show that their
\tau
-cluster morphism category has an associative composition rule
[
BM21
, Corollary 1.8]
by considering several cases.
Igusa–Todorov’s treatment of the representation finite hereditary case makes use of root systems
[
IT17
, Section 1]
.
Our proof takes advantage of the functoriality of silting reduction.

Theorem 4.3
.

The composition rule for
\tcmc_{A}
is associative. Thus
\tcmc_{A}
is a category.

Proof.

Given three composable morphisms

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{S}_{1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{S}_{2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{S}_{3}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{S}_{4}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Q}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R}

we verify the identity

R\circ(Q\circ P)=(R\circ Q)\circ P.

The bijection in (
4.F
) is induced by the functor
\pi_{P}
(and similarly for
\pi_{Q}
), whence we may apply
Corollary

2.13
when expanding the right hand side.

\displaystyle(R\circ Q)\circ P

\displaystyle=(\pi_{Q}^{-1}(R))\circ P

\displaystyle=\pi_{P}^{-1}(\pi_{Q}^{-1}(R))

\displaystyle=\pi^{-1}_{\pi_{P}^{-1}(Q)}(R)

\displaystyle=\pi^{-1}_{Q\circ P}(R)

\displaystyle=R\circ(Q\circ P).

The proof is complete.
∎

Proof.

The morphism set
\tcmc_{A}(\mathcal{S}_{1},\mathcal{S}_{2})
is a subset of
2\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(C_{U})
. On the other hand, the morphism set
\tcmc^{\rm BM}_{H^{0}A}(W_{1},W_{2})
is a subset of
\staurigidpair(W_{1})
, where
W_{i}
is the wide subcategory
\mathcal{S}_{i}\cap\fgMod H^{0}A
of
\fgMod H^{0}A
, for
i\in\{1,2\}
. Using
Theorem

1.17
and (
4.G
), we define a map

(4.I)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tcmc_{A}(\mathcal{S}_{1},\mathcal{S}_{2})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\staurigidpair_{H_{{C_{U}}}({P})}({H^{0}C_{U}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\staurigidpair_{(M,R)}({W_{1}})}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H_{C_{U}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{-1}_{(M,R)}}

It follows from
Proposition

2.9
(
1
) that the
\tau
-perpendicular category of
H_{C_{U}}(P)
in
W_{1}
is
W_{2}
. Consequently, the image of this map is a subset of
\tcmc^{\rm BM}_{H^{0}A}(W_{1},W_{2})
, so a map of Hom-sets has thus been constructed.

It is easy to check that the functor
E
sends identity maps to identity maps; they are given by trivial presilting objects and trivial
\tau
-rigid pairs. It should also be shown that composition is respected. Let
P
and
Q
be a pair of composable morphisms in
\tcmc_{A}
, as shown in (
4.E
). Their composite is then given by
{V=}\pi_{P}^{-1}(Q)
. Let
(M,R)
denote the
\tau
-rigid pair
{H_{{C_{U}}}}({P})
in
\fgMod H^{0}C_{U}
. Consider the following diagram of bijections:

(4.J)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 2\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}_{{P}}({C_{U}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\staurigidpair_{H_{{C_{U}}}({P})}({H^{0}C_{U}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\staurigidpair_{(M,R)}({W_{1}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{2_{{T^{+}_{P}}}\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}({\mathcal{Z}_{P}/[P]})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 2\mathchar 45\relax\mathrm{presilt}(C_{V})}

E
full, we fix an element
